title: Stream JSON log viewer with filtered views for AI agent output
description:
Add a frontend log display mode for jobs that produce Claude CLI stream-json output (--output-format stream-json). The raw log is NDJSON with multiple event types:

- type: system (init metadata — session_id, tools, model, etc.)
- type: assistant with content[].type: text (AI agent's thinking/response text)
- type: assistant with content[].type: tool_use (tool calls — name, input params)
- type: user with content[].type: tool_result (tool call results)
- type: result (final summary — success/error, cost, usage stats)

The viewer should support filter modes:
1. RAW — current behavior, show full log as-is
2. MESSAGES — show only the AI's text responses (assistant events where content contains type: text). Strip the JSON wrapper and display the text field directly. This gives a clean conversation view.
3. TOOL CALLS — show assistant tool_use events as expandable cards (tool name as header, input params collapsed by default). Optionally pair with the corresponding tool_result.
4. ALL PARSED — show all events in a structured timeline with type badges, expandable JSON details

Detection: auto-detect stream-json format by checking if the first line of the log parses as JSON with a type field. If detected, offer the filter toggle. If not, fall back to raw display.

Example data structure from a real run is documented in the ticket discussion.

title: Configurable per-job concurrency — allow multiple simultaneous instances
description:
## Problem

Currently, the `active_runs` HashMap in the daemon is keyed by `job_id`, meaning only one instance of a job can run at a time. If a job's schedule fires while a previous run is still active, the old RunHandle is silently overwritten, potentially orphaning the previous run (which may appear as Killed).

This is a blocker for multi-tenant use cases such as AI chat/agent systems where the same job definition (e.g. an 'agent' job) needs to serve multiple tenants simultaneously.

## Proposed Solution

Add a per-job boolean field `allow_concurrent` (default: `false`) that controls whether multiple simultaneous runs of a single job are permitted.

### Current Behavior (keep as-is when allow_concurrent = false)
- Only one run per job at a time
- If a new run starts while one is active, the previous run is killed
- This is the existing behavior and remains the default

### New Behavior (when allow_concurrent = true)
- Multiple runs of the same job can execute simultaneously with no cap
- Change `active_runs` from `HashMap<Uuid, RunHandle>` (keyed by job_id) to support multiple runs per job (e.g. keyed by run_id, or `HashMap<Uuid, Vec<RunHandle>>`)
- Ensure kill/shutdown logic handles multiple active runs per job
- Update API endpoints (create/update job) to accept the new field

### Out of Scope
- Capping the number of concurrent instances (no max_instances limit)
- Changing the kill-on-overlap behavior for non-concurrent jobs

### Frontend Changes
- Add `allow_concurrent` toggle/checkbox to the job creation/edit form
- Default: off (false)

## Use Case

AI agent/chat systems where a single job definition (the 'agent') is shared across multiple tenants who may trigger it concurrently.

title: CLI update command and version check in status
description:
## Summary

Add a self-update mechanism to ACS and enhance the status command with version awareness.

## Requirements

### 1. Fix hardcoded version
- The health endpoint in `acs/src/server/health.rs` hardcodes version as `"0.1.0"` instead of reading from Cargo.toml
- Replace with `env!("CARGO_PKG_VERSION")` so the version stays in sync automatically

### 2. Enhance `status` command with latest version check
- The `status` command already displays `Version: 0.1.0` from the health endpoint
- Add a check against the GitHub releases API (`https://api.github.com/repos/Jtonna/agent-cron-scheduler/releases/latest`) to fetch the latest released version
- If a newer version is available, display it alongside the current version, e.g.:
  ```
  Version:     0.1.0 (update available: 1.6.0)
  ```
- If already on latest or the check fails (no internet, rate limited), degrade gracefully — just show current version

### 3. New `update` CLI command
- Add an `update` subcommand to the CLI
- Should download the latest release from GitHub releases for the current platform (Windows .exe, macOS .dmg, Linux .AppImage)
- Update both the ACS binary and the bundled webapp
- The release workflow already builds platform-specific artifacts and attaches them to GitHub releases
- Should show download progress and confirm before replacing
- Handle edge cases: already on latest version, no releases found, network errors

## Key files
- `acs/src/cli/mod.rs` — CLI command definitions
- `acs/src/cli/daemon.rs` — status command implementation (line ~275)
- `acs/src/server/health.rs` — health endpoint with hardcoded version (line 46)
- `acs/Cargo.toml` — package version
- `.github/workflows/release.yml` — release artifact naming convention

## Notes
- The project uses `reqwest` already as a dependency, which can be used for the GitHub API calls
- Release artifacts follow the pattern: `AgentCronScheduler-{tag}-{platform}.{ext}`
- The repo is at `Jtonna/agent-cron-scheduler` on GitHub
close_reason: Implemented: version bump to 1.6.0, health.rs env! macro, openapi sync, release script updates, status version check, update CLI command, release workflow raw binaries, documentation updates, full test coverage.

comments.author: Jacob Tonna
comments.text:
## Real-world update flow (Linux WSL reference)

The following steps were manually performed to update from v1.5.4 to v1.6.0 on Linux WSL. The update command should automate the relevant parts of this per-platform.

### Linux update steps observed:
1. Check installed version: `agentcronsystem --version`
2. Check latest release: `gh release list --repo Jtonna/agent-cron-scheduler --limit 1`
3. Kill old daemon process (via PID file at `~/.local/share/agent-cron-scheduler/agentcronsystem.pid`)
4. Kill old GUI processes (`pkill -f squashfs-root`, `pkill -f acsapp`)
5. Remove old files (old binary symlink, old AppImage, extracted dirs)
6. Download new release AppImage from GitHub releases
7. Install: `chmod +x` and copy to `~/.local/bin/AgentCronScheduler`
8. Launch new GUI: `DISPLAY=:0 AgentCronScheduler &>/dev/null & disown`
9. Start daemon (if GUI didn't auto-start): find embedded binary in AppImage mount, run `agentcronsystem start --foreground`
10. Verify old processes gone, new ones running, daemon healthy

### Platform considerations:
- **Linux**: AppImage-based. Kill processes, download new AppImage, replace, relaunch.
- **Windows**: Uses .exe installer. May need to stop daemon service, run new installer silently/in background, restart. The Electron app bundles the Rust binary.
- **macOS**: Uses .dmg. Similar stop/replace/restart flow.

### Design notes:
- The `update` command runs from the CLI (the Rust binary), so it needs to handle replacing itself
- On Windows, the binary may be locked while running — may need to spawn an updater process that waits for the current process to exit, then replaces files
- Should handle both service-installed and manual-start scenarios
- The GUI (Electron app) bundles the binary, so updating the GUI also updates the binary
- Ideally the update runs in the background with minimal user disruption
- Consider: should `update` update just the CLI binary, just the GUI/installer, or both? User wants BOTH.

comments.author: Jacob Tonna
comments.text:
## Updated approach: Ship raw binaries alongside installers

### Problem with installer-based updates
Running installers (exe/dmg/AppImage) from a CLI update command is messy — platform-specific, disruptive, requires killing GUI processes, and on Windows the installer can't run while the app is open.

### New approach: Raw binaries in releases
The GitHub release workflow should attach TWO types of artifacts per platform:

1. **Installers** (for first-time install, existing):
   - Windows: `AgentCronScheduler-{version}-windows.exe`
   - macOS: `AgentCronScheduler-{version}-mac.dmg`
   - Linux: `AgentCronScheduler-{version}-linux.AppImage`

2. **Raw binaries** (for self-update, NEW):
   - Windows: `agentcronsystem-{version}-windows.exe` (Rust daemon) + `AgentCronScheduler-{version}-windows-portable.zip` (Electron app unpacked)
   - macOS: `agentcronsystem-{version}-macos` + equivalent Electron binary
   - Linux: `agentcronsystem-{version}-linux` + equivalent Electron binary

### Simplified update flow (all platforms):
1. `agentcronsystem update` checks GitHub API for latest release
2. Downloads the raw binaries for current platform
3. Stops the running daemon gracefully
4. Replaces the binary files in-place (or next to current location)
5. Spawns the new daemon binary
6. Old process exits

### Key benefit:
- Consistent across all platforms
- No installer execution needed
- No GUI process management
- The old Rust binary can just exec/spawn the new one and exit
- On Windows: avoids file-locking issues since we stop the daemon first, replace, then start new

### Release workflow changes needed:
- Modify `.github/workflows/release.yml` to also upload raw compiled binaries as separate release assets
- Name them distinctly from the installer artifacts so the update command knows which to download

### Scope update:
This ticket now covers:
1. Fix hardcoded version in health.rs (`env!("CARGO_PKG_VERSION")`)
2. Enhance `status` with latest version check from GitHub
3. New `update` CLI command using raw binary replacement
4. Modify release workflow to include raw binaries as release assets

comments.author: Jacob Tonna
comments.text:
## Version consistency: all version references must stay in sync

### Current problem
The version is defined in multiple places and they are out of sync:
- `acs/Cargo.toml` — `version = "0.1.0"` (Rust package version)
- `acs/src/server/health.rs` line 46 — hardcoded `"0.1.0"` string in health endpoint
- `acs/web/openapi.yaml` — `version: "0.1.0"` in the info section
- `electron/package.json` — `"version": "1.6.0"` (Electron app version)
- `electron/packages/app/package.json` — `"version": "1.6.0"` (Electron app package)

The Rust side says 0.1.0 while the Electron/release side says 1.6.0. These need to be unified.

### Requirements
1. **Single source of truth** — decide where the version lives (likely `electron/package.json` since the release script bumps it there, or `Cargo.toml`)
2. **health.rs** — must use `env!("CARGO_PKG_VERSION")` instead of hardcoded string
3. **openapi.yaml** — the info.version should match the actual release version, either:
   - Dynamically injected at build time (build.rs), or
   - Kept in sync by the release script, or
   - Served dynamically by the Rust server (replace static file serving with a handler that injects version)
4. **Cargo.toml** — should match the release version (currently 0.1.0 vs 1.6.0)
5. **release.sh** — the release script already bumps electron/package.json files. It should also bump Cargo.toml and openapi.yaml (or those should derive from a single source)

### Acceptance criteria
- All version references return the same value
- `agentcronsystem status` shows the correct release version
- Swagger UI info section shows the correct release version
- `agentcronsystem --version` shows the correct release version
- The release script updates ALL version locations in one go

title: ACS WebUI: Remote instance switcher with dropdown + saved connections
description:
The ACS frontend needs the ability to connect to multiple remote ACS instances from the WebUI.

## Requirements

- Store previously connected instances (persist across sessions)

close_reason: Implemented remote instance switcher for ACS WebUI: SavedConnection types + localStorage CRUD, refactored getBaseUrl() for active connection priority, created useInstanceHealth hook for remote health checks and version compatibility, built InstanceDialog component for add/edit connections with validation, replaced SidebarHeader with instance switcher dropdown showing local and saved remote connections with status indicators, and added edit/delete context actions for connection management. comments.author: Jacob Tonna
comments.text:
Clarification responses for autonomous execution:

1. Connection architecture: Direct browser connection. The frontend will change the base URL for API calls to point at the remote instance. Remote ACS instances will need to serve appropriate CORS headers.

2. Persistence mechanism: Browser localStorage. Saved connections are per-browser, simple key-value storage.

3. Authentication and trust: No authentication required. Trust the local network — if you can reach the instance, you can connect.

4. Instance switching behavior: Reload and redirect to home. When switching instances, clear the current view and redirect to the dashboard, loading fresh data from the new instance.

5. Error handling for unreachable instances: Inline dropdown indicator. Show a status dot (red/green) next to each instance name in the dropdown so users can see at a glance which instances are reachable.

6. Version compatibility: Block on major version mismatch. Allow minor version differences but prevent connecting to instances with incompatible major versions. Show an error explaining the version requirement.

title: Job lifecycle hooks — before, during, and after execution
description: Research and design a hooks system for ACS jobs. Three hook types: pre-execution (before job starts — validate preconditions, acquire locks), during-execution (monitor live output, pattern matching, interactive stdin), post-execution (cleanup, notifications, job chaining). Key questions: what form do hooks take (shell commands, other ACS jobs, plugins)? Per-job vs global config? Failure propagation? Interaction with PTY/SSE streaming? Relationship to ENH-002 output parsing? Expected output: design document, data model changes, API surface, complexity estimate.
